narrative.overview:
This is a clean, conventional developer portfolio, chosen on purpose as the category standard and held to a very high level of craft. The name is a plain description of the system: flat surfaces, 1px rules for structure, and one vermilion accent on white and light grey sections. The quality bar is the craft of Brittany Chiang's portfolio, Josh Comeau's site and Linear. None of them is a template to copy.

Because the form is familiar, finish does the work: heavy, tightly tracked headings, a shared column split, consistent control heights, considered states. Density is comfortable and made for scanning, with the detail available to anyone who reads on. The few distinctive behaviours all help navigation: a layer name that stays in view, a project highlighted once on arrival, and a nav wordmark that waits until the hero has scrolled away.

Light is the default and the reference. Dark is an opt-in preference, saved in the browser and never taken from the operating system, and it keeps the same structure. The system rejects eyebrows above headings, generic stat rows and walls of tags.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, structured by 1px rules and whitespace, with no cards
One vermilion accent, on white and light grey by default
One typeface, Schibsted Grotesk, with heavy, tightly tracked headings
The statement is the largest thing on the page, and the name stays small
Behaviour that helps orientation: the layer rail, the arrival highlight, the deferred wordmark
One scroll-driven moment: the stack band, with faint logos that never sit behind reading text

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is the only accent hue in the system. It marks list markers, current location and hover, and at rest it never fills a button, a link or a section. Actions are ink, so the red stays rare. A new meaning gets a neutral treatment, not a second accent.

rules.name: The Opt-in Dark Rule
rules.body: Light is what every visitor sees first. Dark appears only after a visitor chooses it with the toggle, and any new colour is defined for both themes.

rules.name: The Statement Over Name Rule
rules.body: The largest type states what Peter does. His name and title sit above it at lede size, as a plain byline in sentence case, with the name in weight 800 and the title in muted.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No heading has a small label above it, in any form: no kickers, no tracked uppercase, no section numbers. A heading starts its own section, and any supporting line goes below it. The hero byline is the single identity line named by the rule above and is not a pattern to repeat.

rules.name: The Heavy Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings are weight 800 with negative tracking, tighter as they get larger. Tracking is never positive, and nothing is set in uppercase.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk is the only family. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and the ink and muted pair.

rules.name: The Layer Rail Rule
rules.body: A layer's name is always visible while its projects scroll. On wide screens the header sticks in the left column, 1.5rem below the nav. Once stacked, the title alone pins directly under the nav on a page-coloured strip, and entries get a scroll margin so a jump lands clear of it.

rules.name: The First Mention Rule
rules.body: A project's summary, metadata and stack appear once, under the first layer it belongs to. Later layers show only what was done in that layer, with links back to its other layers.

rules.name: The Flat And Ruled Rule
rules.body: Content has no cards, boxes, or resting shadows. When two things need separating, use space first, then a 1px rule. A blurred shadow is only for something that floats above the content. Section grounds are the one exception: Experience and Skills and education sit on Page Alt, and Contact is a full-width field of ink that closes the page. Between white and Page Alt the page ground fades over 0.5s when a tone section reaches mid-screen, including the nav. Contact is always a sharp edge, because text has to flip from dark to light there. With reduced motion or no JavaScript, tone sections stay as sharp bands.

rules.name: The Deferred Wordmark Rule
rules.body: The hero already names Peter, so the nav wordmark stays hidden while the hero byline is on screen and fades in once it has scrolled under the nav. Without JavaScript the wordmark is always visible.

rules.name: The Once Only Rule
rules.body: The highlight plays once per arrival and never loops, pulses or responds to hover. It exists to confirm where a jump landed.

rules.name: The Clear Column Rule
rules.body: Decoration lives in the hero, the band, the empty rail and the bottom of Contact. It never sits behind a project's text, Experience, About or Skills.

dos: **Do** separate content with whitespace and 1px rules, using Line Strong for structure and Line within a block.
**Do** align new labelled content to the 0.7 to 1.6 split so the content column keeps its left edge.
**Do** define every new colour for both themes.
**Do** use the shared 0.2s ease-out for state changes, and keep hover to colour and border.
**Do** make every button and nav control at least 2.75rem tall, and give every new motion a reduced-motion fallback.
**Do** keep the page working without JavaScript, as the nav links and wordmark do today.
donts: **Don't** put an eyebrow, kicker or small label above a heading.
**Don't** put content in cards or give it a resting shadow.
**Don't** add a second accent or typeface.
**Don't** make dark the default or follow the operating system's theme.
**Don't** make the name larger than the statement, or show the nav wordmark while the hero byline is on screen.
**Don't** add a generic stat row or a wall of tags. Skills stay as plain text.
**Don't** lift or move anything on hover. Controls respond with colour and border, plus a 1px press.
**Don't** repeat a project's summary and stack in a later layer, or loop the arrival highlight.
**Don't** put logos or patterns behind reading text, or mix brand logos and generic shapes in one set.
